title: Why Black Swan Events Defy Forecasts
title_options: What Taleb Means by a Black Swan
Why Hindsight Makes Black Swans Look Predictable
One Black Swan Can Shatter a Forecast
description: What does Nassim Taleb mean by a Black Swan? This Q Station Short explains the idea: a Black Swan is an event outside normal expectations, with enormous impact, that people often make look predictable in hindsight. The metaphor comes from the old European belief that all swans were white until Europeans encountered black swans in Australia. The practical lesson is that forecasts built from past observations can miss consequential surprises in markets, technology, and beyond. Taleb's response is not perfect prediction, but less dependence on fragile forecasts and more room for error. Q Station explores questions that open bigger worlds of ideas.

body: A Black Swan is an event outside normal expectations.
Afterward, people build explanations that make it look predictable.
Hindsight hides how surprising it really was.
The name comes from Europe's old belief that all swans were white.
Then Europeans encountered black swans in Australia.
One observation shattered a rule that had seemed certain.
Taleb says forecasts can fail the same way.
Models usually depend on what has already been observed.
Markets can change through events those models barely considered.
Technologies can overturn assumptions just as suddenly.
You cannot reliably predict every Black Swan.
So reduce dependence on fragile forecasts.
Leave room for error before surprise arrives.
